I'm an engineering student at Harvey Mudd College. I like working where hardware and software meet: designing digital logic, figuring out how processors work, and writing the low-level code that brings a board to life.

## What I Study

- **Computer architecture.** How processors are built and what makes them fast. For my System-on-Chip Design final project, my partner and I turned a single-cycle RISC-V core into a 5-stage pipelined processor and optimized it for speed and area.
- **Digital design and verification.** Writing SystemVerilog and proving it works, using simulation, compliance tests, and benchmarks. As a Clay-Wolkin Research Fellow, I wrote certification tests for the RISC-V Sdtrig debug extension.
- **Embedded systems.** Programming microcontrollers at the register level and connecting them to real peripherals. In Microprocessor-based Systems (E155), I've worked with an iCE40 FPGA and an STM32L432KC microcontroller, building keypad scanners, digital audio, and an SPI temperature sensor served over Wi-Fi.
- **Hardware in industry.** At TRL11, I worked on space-qualified networking hardware.

## On This Site

- [Labs](labs.qmd): write-ups for my E155 labs, covering design, testing, and results.
